# Ridge regression 

## Set up problem 

-   Abalone data set

-   Issue with multicollinearity

-   Variances will be high (show X\^TX matrix)

What if we want to keep all the predictors in the model?

## Ridge regression 

-   show optimization

-   describe the penalty

-   what is happening as lambda goes to 0? What about as lambda goes to infinity? (We'll talk about how to find lambda later)

-   We will use standardized predictors for ridge regression. why does this matter?

## Estimator 

-   you found this in exam 01

-   Is it an unbiased estimator?

-   what is the variance? - this may be too long for class?

-   This is the bias-variance trade off - we accept a little bias in order to reduce the variance

## When is ridge useful 

Most useful for models in which the SE of OLS are large and unstable but you want to keep all the predictors

-   That lambda I term helps stablize the variance when x\^tX is nearly singular.

-   So this is the case when there is high multicollinearity

-   when P is close to n

-   Makes it possible to estimate coefficients when p \> n (is this true)?

## LImitations 

-   Ridge will not ever set the coefficients to exactly equal to 0 (limitation if you want to reduce the number of coefficients in th emodel)

    -   Similar method called LASSO that addresses this

## data


::: {.cell layout-align="center"}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(tidyverse)
library(tidymodels)
library(rms)

nba_salaries <- read_csv("data/nba-salaries-2022-23.csv")

nba_salaries <- nba_salaries |>
  mutate(PG = if_else(Position == "PG", TRUE, FALSE))

nba_salaries <- nba_salaries |>
  select(-Position,  -`Player Name`) 

nba_salaries_scaled <- nba_salaries |>
  mutate(across(-Salary, ~ if(is.numeric(.)) scale(.) else .))

model1 <- lm(Salary ~ ., data = nba_salaries)
tidy(model1)
```

```{.r .cell-code}
# pass standardized data in: 
ridge_fit <- MASS::lm.ridge(Salary ~ 0 + ., data = nba_salaries_scaled,
                           lambda = 5000)

beta_scaled_lmridge <-  ridge_fit$coef # scaled space coefficients
beta_unscaled_lmridge <-  coef(ridge_fit) # original scale coefficients 

# (different than computed above if y and X are not standardized inputs)

tidy(ridge_fit)
```
